title: A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms Is Coming To Save Fantasy TV
text:
Angel Shaw is a New TV Lead Writer with ScreenRant who knows far too much about the worlds of Harry Potter and The Lord of the Rings.
HBO's newest Game of Thrones series, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, is on its way to save fantasy TV. Of course, there's no question that the original Game of Thrones TV show revolutionized the genre.
The massive-scale project demonstrated to audiences and production companies alike just how spectacular fantasy TV could be. It's no surprise, then, that several similar projects have arrived on screens, though they have often fallen flat. The TV industry's desperate attempts to duplicate Game of Thrones have, by now, become quite tiresome. In the effort, fantasy TV has become something rather different. It seems that every new show is trying to match that intense political intrigue and harsh brutality. Gone are the days of more traditional fantasy adventures. Hopefully, however, as the Game of Thrones franchise takes a new approach, it can again revolutionize the genre. The Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms Stories Balance GOT Brutality With Classic Fantasy Adventure George R. R. Martin's A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms isn't quite like his other A Song of Ice and Fire books. Sure, there's plenty of the author's familiar flair, but the overall format and themes are more like traditional fantasy. Dunk is a classic underdog hero, more chivalrous than the celebrated knights, but not born to high status. It's an age-old trope, but blended with the harsh world of Game of Thrones. Based on the trailers for A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, we can assume that the upcoming TV show will be similarly different from Game of Thrones. It appears to be a smaller-scale adventure—less about political maneuvers and more about those exciting, poetic, and heartwarming elements that fantasy used to be known for. We can undoubtedly expect brutality and gore, but there should be a greater balance. This New Game Of Thrones Series Can Begin A New Era In Fantasy TV There's little chance that A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms will be as massive a success as Game of Thrones. It may not even really compete with House of the Dragon, which has a similar large-scale political approach as its predecessor. Regardless, this new HBO show can impact the fantasy genre's trajectory. If Dunk and Egg's stories resonate with viewers, then we can again see other production companies and streaming platforms attempt to duplicate that success. It could mean a wave of more traditional fantasy adventures. Underdog heroes, chivalrous deeds, and heartwarming themes may be brought to the screen in balance with that heart-pumping brutality. A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms could mean a new era in fantasy television.
